name: Razer Phone
pros: Wi-Fi support (Wi-Fi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac, dual-band, Wi-Fi Direct, hotspot) for data-free browsing and connectivity
8 MP, f/2.0 camera capable of capturing good photos for its release era
Snapdragon 835 chipset provides balanced everyday performance
Li-Po 4000 mAh battery offers solid operating endurance for daily use
cons: Standard charging speeds without ultra-fast charging support

reviews.title: Solid performance for its 2017 launch era
reviews.body: Picking this up around its release period, the Android 7.1.1, up to Android 9.0 experience felt snappy and responsive for the price tier. The 8 MP, f/2.0 camera delivered reliable shots in outdoor lighting.

reviews.title: Reliable battery and daily usability
reviews.body: The Li-Po 4000 mAh power cell paired with Razer's software tuning easily lasted through a full work day with mixed web browsing, calls, and media playback.

reviews.title: Refined hardware styling and build
reviews.body: The physical chassis of the Razer Phone feels well-balanced in hand. Its 158.5 x 77.7 x 8 mm (6.24 x 3.06 x 0.31 in) make it easy to hold during long daily sessions.

reviews.title: Great value for the hardware specifications
reviews.body: For the price point, getting Snapdragon 835 performance alongside 64GB storage, microSDXC made the Razer Phone an easy recommendation among rivals in 2017.

reviews.title: Smooth day-to-day software responsiveness
reviews.body: Operating on Android 7.1.1, up to Android 9.0, the user interface is intuitive with smooth system transitions. Core apps and browsing run without noticeable stutter.

reviews.title: Dependable display and audio clarity
reviews.body: The screen (Li-Po 4000 mAh, non-removable, 5.7", 1440x2560 pixels) produces vibrant colors for video streaming, and call clarity through the earpiece is crystal clear.

reviews.title: A well-rounded package from Razer
reviews.body: Overall, the Razer Phone proved to be a durable and well-engineered mobile device representing Razer's design philosophy nicely.
